summary: Globes profiles Eylon Levy, a 32-year-old London-born government spokesperson to the international media, who became widely known after a Sky News interview with Kay Burley during the Israel-Hamas war. He describes the questions he faces, the information war over Gaza, and the coordinated work of the National Public Diplomacy Directorate. He also recounts his path from debating at Oxford and Cambridge to immigrating to Israel, and he calls for national unity after October 7.
one_line: Profile of Eylon Levy, London-born Israeli government spokesperson to the international media, whose Sky News interview went viral during the Israel-Hamas war.
key_facts: Eylon Levy, aged 32, was born and raised in London to parents who had moved there from Israel, and is a government spokesperson to the international media at the National Public Diplomacy Directorate in the Prime Minister's Office.
As a child Levy watched then Israeli ambassador to the UK Mark Regev on television and wanted to be a spokesperson for Israel; he now works TV shifts alongside Regev.

In a Sky News interview, Kay Burley asked Levy whether Israel's willingness to release 150 Palestinian prisoners for 50 Israeli hostages showed it thinks Palestinian lives are worth less; Levy called it a "disgusting accusation".
Levy's tweet of the Sky News clip received 16 million views and 15,000 shares, and his followers rose from 24,000 before the war to 140,000.
His astonished look and raised eyebrows became a popular meme and WhatsApp sticker.

The National Public Diplomacy Directorate is headed by Moshe Aviv and works with Israel Police, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the IDF Spokesperson, the Israel Prisons Service, the Shin Bet, the National Security Council and the Ministry of Diaspora Affairs.
Levy says he did interviews around the clock, including four BBC interviews on one Saturday and a CNN interview at 2am; Tal Heinrich handles prime-time interviews in the US.
Levy cites the Al-Ahli hospital claim of 800 civilians killed as a Hamas lie, which he says was actually hit by a splinter group of Islamic Jihad and no hospital was destroyed.
He argues that the war is also an information war and that reporters in Gaza operate under a dictatorial regime and cannot show terrorists, missile launches or the Hamas tunnels under Shifa.

In 2013, as an Oxford undergraduate, Levy debated MP George Galloway, who left saying 'I don't do debates with Israelis. Goodbye' after learning Levy was Israeli; it was covered by UK media and a cartoon in The Times.
After completing a master's degree in international relations at Cambridge in 2014, Levy immigrated to Israel and enlisted in the army at 23, reporting to the Tel Hashomer induction center.

Levy served in the command center of the IDF coordinator of activities in the administered territories, then worked as a newsreader for the Israel Broadcasting Authority and i24News, was foreign media advisor to President Isaac Herzog until May 2023, and has translated some 30 books from Hebrew to English.
Levy took part in the protests against the government's judicial reform, and says that after October 7 the only task is to win the war and unite.
